G1.title: Position sizing (field 14)
G1.text: Planned stop risk = 1% of current strategy equity per position: quantity = (0.01 x equity) / (|entry - stop| + estimated round-trip cost per unit). Provisional caps (need approval): gross leverage at most 3x; per-symbol notional at most 25% of equity; at most 4 concurrent positions per strategy; daily loss limit 3% of equity (flat and halt until the next UTC day); halve risk at -15% from peak, halt for review at -25%. The 1% applies per position, with portfolio-level caps separate. Realized loss can exceed 1% (gaps, slippage, liquidation); enforce margin, minimum-order and lot-size limits.

G2.title: Fees, slippage and execution (field 17)
G2.text: Signal on a closed bar t; execute at the open of t+1 as a taker order (long at ask-side reference, short at bid-side; with OHLCV only, open plus or minus an estimated half-spread). Fee and slippage figures are ESTIMATES until verified in Phase 2: 5 bps taker fee + 2 bps slippage per side = 14 bps round trip (base). Scenarios with multipliers declared before any test: Base 14 bps RT; Adverse 22 bps RT (about 1.6x); Stress 35 bps RT (2.5x) with doubled stop slippage; extra sensitivity point at 11 bps RT. Stops are stop-market: fill at the stop plus slippage; a gap through the stop fills at the worse of stop and open. If stop and target are both touched inside one candle, assume the stop hit first (conservative) unless higher-resolution data resolve the order. No limit-order fills are assumed; maker variants need their own fill model. Flag a strategy EXECUTION-SENSITIVE if profit disappears under Adverse costs.

G3.title: Funding treatment (field 18)
G3.text: Perps: apply realized funding at the actual payment timestamps (00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC unless the symbol differs; verify per symbol) to the position held at those times. A funding signal (percentile, premium) is distinct from payments actually paid or received. Use realized history only, never future funding. Strategies that ignore funding as a signal still pay or receive it in P&L. Spot or equity legs: no funding.

G4.title: Validation protocol (field 24)
G4.text: Sequential gates 1 to 7 (G7 below). Chronological splits only: train, validation, walk-forward (at least 4 folds, expanding or rolling), then one final holdout (last 20% of effective history) opened once after the specification is frozen. Embargo at least the maximum holding period; purge overlapping labels. Six months is the default window, not enough for a holdout plus walk-forward on slow strategies: use all verified history, otherwise mark INCONCLUSIVE. Automated causality tests: truncation (signals at t unchanged when data end at t), shift, HTF-closed-bar and pivot-delay tests. Experiment registry records every variant, parameter set and rejection. Multiple testing: Deflated Sharpe, Benjamini-Hochberg across the strategy family, PBO (CSCV) where applicable. Dependence-aware bootstrap (stationary or block) for Sharpe, expectancy and drawdown. Benchmarks: buy-and-hold and a random-entry null with identical exit, hold and costs. Parameter-plateau analysis, regime breakdown, cross-asset and cross-timeframe robustness.

G5.title: Minimum data (field 25)
G5.text: At least 6 complete calendar months plus warm-up of 3x the longest lookback. Approximate bars in 6 months: 5m about 52,000; 15m about 17,500; 1h about 4,400. Provisional trade counts: at least 100 in the full sample and 30 out of sample; fewer gives INCONCLUSIVE, not REJECT. Extra data needs are in each sheet's data line.

G6.title: Diagnostic plots (field 27)
G6.text: Equity curve; benchmark comparison; drawdown curve; monthly returns; rolling Sharpe (when the sample allows); trade-return distribution; long vs short; performance by instrument and timeframe; by market regime; cost sensitivity; parameter sensitivity; walk-forward results. All from computed data, never synthetic. Exports: trade log, equity and drawdown series, metrics table, configuration, data provenance, validation results, reproducibility metadata.

G7.title: Acceptance and rejection (fields 28 and 29)
G7.text: Gate 1 data validity; 2 causality; 3 implementation; 4 economic viability; 5 statistical reliability; 6 robustness; 7 operational readiness. PROVISIONAL thresholds (need your approval; check against the repo's validation contract): net expectancy at least 20 bps per trade under Base costs (screening policy, not a detectability claim); still net positive under Adverse costs; at least 4 of 5 walk-forward folds profitable; P95 bootstrap max drawdown under 35%; at least 60% positive months; worst month no worse than -15%; Deflated Sharpe probability at least 0.95. REJECT on any failure of Gates 2 or 3, non-positive net expectancy under Base costs, or dependence on one fold or one regime. INCONCLUSIVE when sample or power is inadequate. EXECUTION-SENSITIVE when profit exists only under Base costs. BLOCKED when required data are unavailable.

strategies.name: Moving-average trend continuation
strategies.rationale: Slow information diffusion and herding create serial correlation that slow moving averages capture.
strategies.instruments: BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, SUI, JUP USDT-M perps (per-symbol history to be verified)
strategies.long_entry: EMA(20) crosses above EMA(100) at bar close while close > EMA(200); enter next bar open.
strategies.short_entry: Mirror image of the long rules (two-sided variant, tested as a separate hypothesis from long-only).
strategies.exit: Opposite EMA(20)/EMA(100) cross, or 2 consecutive closes beyond EMA(100) against the position.
strategies.stop_loss: 2*ATR(14) from entry, fixed at entry (ATR taken from the signal bar); trailing 3*ATR variant declared as a separate test.
strategies.frequency: One entry per signal episode (no re-entry while the condition persists); cool-down 5 bars after an exit; max 1 open position per symbol
strategies.no_trade: ADX(14) < 15; ATR(14) below its 10th percentile of 200 bars; data gap in the last 5 bars.
strategies.hypothesis: EMA(20/100) crosses with the EMA(200) filter earn positive net expectancy after Base costs and beat buy-and-hold on risk-adjusted terms inside trending sub-periods.
strategies.failure_modes: Whipsaw in ranges; cost drag on 5m; late entries; regime dependence.
strategies.fixed_rules: Cross rule, EMA(200) filter, next-bar execution, ATR stop at entry.
strategies.calibrate: Fast in {10,20,30}, slow in {50,100,150} (small grid, training and validation only).
strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.rationale: A stacked EMA order shows persistent direction; expanding volatility shows participation rather than drift.

strategies.long_entry: EMA(10) > EMA(30) > EMA(100) and close > EMA(10), with ATR(14) above its 50-bar median; enter on the first bar the full condition turns true.
strategies.short_entry: Mirror image of the long rules (two-sided variant, tested as a separate hypothesis from long-only).

strategies.frequency: One entry per signal episode (no re-entry while the condition persists); cool-down 5 bars after an exit; max 1 open position per symbol
strategies.no_trade: ATR(14) below its 30th percentile of 200 bars; EMA(10)/EMA(100) spread under 0.2*ATR (flat stack).
strategies.hypothesis: Requiring ATR expansion removes low-participation whipsaws and raises expectancy against the same alignment without the filter.

strategies.rationale: Breaks of N-bar extremes mark liquidity-seeking moves and trend initiation.

strategies.fixed_rules: Prior-bar channel (no current bar), next-bar execution.
strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.name: Time-series momentum
strategies.rationale: The sign of an asset's own past return predicts near-term continuation (documented across assets; time-varying in crypto).
strategies.instruments: BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, SUI, JUP USDT-M perps (per-symbol history to be verified)
strategies.long_entry: z = R(L) / (sigma * sqrt(L)) with L = 96 bars is above +1 and the 20-bar return is positive.
strategies.short_entry: Mirror image of the long rules (two-sided variant, tested as a separate hypothesis from long-only).
strategies.exit: z crosses back through 0, or max hold reached.
strategies.frequency: One entry per signal episode (no re-entry while the condition persists); cool-down 5 bars after an exit; max 1 open position per symbol
strategies.no_trade: |z| < 1; volatility above its 95th percentile of 500 bars.
strategies.hypothesis: The sign of the volatility-normalized lookback return predicts the next L/4 bars net of costs.
strategies.failure_modes: Short-horizon reversals; sign of autocorrelation flips.
strategies.fixed_rules: Volatility normalization, trade only on signal change.
strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.rationale: ADX separates trending from ranging states, so directional signals act only when trend strength is present.

strategies.hypothesis: Gating DI signals by ADX > 25 improves expectancy over the ungated DI cross.
strategies.failure_modes: ADX lag (late entries); whipsaw near the threshold.
strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.rationale: The higher timeframe sets the dominant drift; lower-timeframe timing shortens stops and entry cost.

strategies.long_entry: HTF EMA(50) > EMA(200) on closed HTF bars only, and LTF EMA(20) crosses above EMA(50).

strategies.name: Trend pullback continuation
strategies.rationale: Pullbacks to dynamic support inside a trend offer better reward-to-risk than breakout entries.
strategies.instruments: BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, SUI, JUP USDT-M perps (per-symbol history to be verified)
strategies.long_entry: EMA(50) > EMA(200); price retraces to within 0.5*ATR of EMA(20), then a bar closes above the prior bar's high.
strategies.short_entry: Mirror image of the long rules (two-sided variant, tested as a separate hypothesis from long-only).

strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.rationale: Scaling momentum by realized volatility equalizes risk across regimes and improves risk-adjusted returns versus raw momentum.

strategies.execution_challenges: Taker entry at next-bar open; stop-market slippage in fast moves; costs matter most on 5m

strategies.hypothesis: Volume-confirmed breaks from qualified boxes continue enough to earn positive net expectancy.

strategies.name: OU-process-inspired spread reversion, subject to stationarity testing
strategies.rationale: A stationary spread follows Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics; deviations scaled by the estimated half-life revert.

strategies.hypothesis: Spreads that pass in-sample stationarity tests stay mean-reverting out of sample (tests pass-then-persist).
strategies.failure_modes: Cointegration breakdown; multiplicity across candidate pairs.
strategies.fixed_rules: Beta and OU parameters from past data only.
strategies.calibrate: Estimation window, z entry, p-value cutoff.
